priority: Your work is document-primary, and almost any current computer handles it. The monitor matters more than the computer.

AutoCAD runs one operation at a time, so a fast core matters more than many cores, and almost any current chip drafts smoothly. Drawings with many xrefs and nested blocks want more RAM and fast storage. The monitor matters more than the computer.

Modeling runs one operation at a time — what counts is how fast each core is, not how many. That's what makes Revit, Rhino, and SketchUp feel responsive. Get a modest dedicated GPU for stable viewports. More powerful ones are only needed for visualization.
Visualization runs on the GPU — Enscape, Lumion, D5, and Twinmotion render faster with a more powerful card, and VRAM sets how large a scene you can hold. The CPU only matters for loading scenes.
This build pays for two things at once — a fast core for modeling and a powerful GPU for visualization. Neither can be cheap, so it costs more than either alone.

Rendering uses every core at once, so the number of cores sets your render times — more cores, faster renders. AMD's Ryzen 9 leads, and Threadripper PRO goes further on a dedicated render box. GPU rendering keeps improving, so it's worth a look if you're still CPU-only.
